scope.fixtures: Synthetic writing-project conversation with actual live assistant replies, plus a valid persisted synthetic game. No real user's history was sent.
scope.execution: Host JVM using built product AgentTransport, ModelPresets, PromptBuilder, SharedExperience, Diary, AgentReply and AgentStore. No mock model.
scope.isolation: Independent recall probes suppress alternative recent-chat/fact recall to measure the diary channel. Full AgentRuntime orchestration, Android UI and scheduling were not exercised in this live run.

overlapping_terms_without_event_name.note: Not mentioning the old event is not automatically a failure when the current turn can be answered naturally.

reflection_withheld_control.note: Removing stored reflection did not eliminate invented historical thoughts or game details; generation grounding also needs attention.

interpretation: Light conversational recall is possible when a relevant event is supplied; this sample did not repeatedly turn unrelated dinner talk into diary recitation.
One selected utterance often loses the surrounding topic, while local lexical relevance misses paraphrases. This contributes to poor old-event recall.
Source IDs and program-generated event facts work, but neither guarantees the semantic grounding of free-text reflections or later replies.
Retrospective feelings sometimes become invented past mental states, causes, sensory details or private life. This is more important than making the prose less literary.
No-record and missing-record responses need a clearer uncertainty boundary.
suggested_next_scope_not_implemented: Retain a few source-linked topic cues from the surrounding exchange for retrieval, without creating new user facts or a second memory service.
Tighten the distinction between a current retrospective feeling and unsupported historical details in the memory-generation and recall slots.
Conditionally signal absent recall evidence so the model can ask for a cue rather than confidently claiming memory.
Re-run the same named, paraphrase, unrelated-topic and missing-memory controls after any change.
limits: Small qualitative sample: two styles, two repetitions, one writing episode and one game per run. Counts are observations, not population success rates.
Assessments of naturalness and unsupported detail were reviewed by the coding assistant, not independent human raters.
Date-shifted recent-event views and withheld reflections are labeled diagnostic controls, not actual product-generated storage behavior.
No real-user longitudinal study, physical handset, streaming or UI validation was performed in this live evaluation.
Only the evaluation harness and aggregate report changed; product behavior, Claude's persona files, version and main branch were left unchanged. No release.
